rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim defines an inadvertent oath as a habitual phrase attached to speech, without intending an oath or wanting to swear; no expiation is due.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: لغو اليمين أن يصل الرجل كلامه بأن يحلف

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet ruled that archers’ casual oaths while shooting carry neither expiation nor punishment.
rows.anchor: كلا، أيمان الرماة لغو لا كفارة فيها ولا عقوبة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha identifies idle oaths as words spoken in joking, disputation, quarrels, or without commitment in the heart.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة: أيمان اللغو ما كان في الهزل والمراء والخصومة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd calls conditional self-curses uttered only by the tongue idle oaths; God does not hold a person to them unless the heart intended them, even once.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: هو دعاء الحالف على نفسه كقوله

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the idle oath is an oath whose expiation removes its sin, so the verse means God does not charge the expiated oath with sin.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: هو اليمين المكفر وسمي لغوا لأن الكفارة تسقط منه الإثم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim says an oath about something that one later forgets and then breaks is not held against the person; he cites the lifting of liability for mistakes, forgetfulness, and coercion.
rows.anchor: المغيرة عن إبراهيم: هو الرجل يحلف على الشيء ثم ينسى فيحنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the heart earns means what it resolves, intends, and deliberately undertakes, since the heart’s earning is its commitment and intention.
rows.anchor: أي عزمتم وقصدتم وتعمدتم لأن كسب القلب العقد على الشيء والنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who swears to perform an obligatory act must fulfill it; breaking that oath incurs expiation because the oath reinforced an existing duty.
rows.anchor: فإن كان فرضا عليه فالواجب عليه أن لا يحنث، فإن حنث فعليه الكفارة

rows.speaker: أحد القولين
rows.claim: One reported view requires expiation when a person breaks an oath to perform a voluntary act.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن عليه الكفارة بالحنث فيه

rows.speaker: القول الثاني
rows.claim: The other reported view requires fulfillment of an oath to perform a voluntary act and accepts no substitute.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني: عليه بالوفاء بما قال ولا يجزيه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking an oath about a future permissible act requires expiation by unanimous agreement.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا إذا حنث فيه لزمته الكفارة بلا خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A knowingly false oath about a past event is a ghamus oath that plunges its maker into sin; the author’s school requires expiation.
rows.anchor: فهو اليمين الغموس الذي يغمس صاحبه في الإثم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa says no expiation is due for a knowingly false past oath and treats it as an idle oath.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا يلزمه الكفارة وتحصيله كاللغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swearing by the explicit names of God—Allah, Billah, or Tallah—is an oath inwardly and outwardly; intent is irrelevant and breaking it requires expiation.
rows.anchor: والله وبالله وتالله، فهذه أيمان صريحة ولا يعتبر فيها النية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oaths by divine attributes such as God’s power, greatness, speech, or knowledge follow the same rule as explicit divine names.
rows.anchor: كقوله: وقدرة الله وعظمة الله وكلام الله وعلم الله ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evasive oath formulas count only with intent; if the speaker denies intending an oath, that denial is accepted.
rows.anchor: فإن نوى اليمين كان يمينا، وإن قال: لم أرد به اليمين قبلنا قوله فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Swearing by created things, people, or one’s life is not an oath and creates no expiation, though it is reprehensible.
rows.anchor: فهذا ليس بيمين، ولا يلزم الكفارة بالحنث فيه، وهو يمين مكروه فيه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet forbade swearing by fathers and instructed people to swear by God instead.
rows.anchor: من كان حالفا فليحلف بالله، لا تحلفوا بآبائكم

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: After the Prophet prohibited it, Umar says he never again swore by his father, either deliberately or in quotation.
rows.anchor: قال عمر: فما حلفت بهذا بعد ذاكرا ولا آثرا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses the oath formula la-ʿamruka; the excerpt gives the line as poetic linguistic evidence without identifying its author.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر منهم: لعمرك ما أخشى التصعلك ما بقا … على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase if you are believers qualifies the command to abandon the remaining usury, as in the parallel phrase you are superior if you are believers.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم إذا كنتم مؤمنين كقوله: وأنتم الأعلون إن كنتم

rows.speaker: الأعمش وعاصم وحمزة رواية أبي بكر
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, ʿAsim in Abu Bakr’s transmission, and Hamza read fa-ādh inū with a long initial vowel.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعمش وعاصم وحمزة رواية أبي بكر فآذنوا ممدودا

rows.speaker: علي وأبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: The short-vowel fa-adh inū reading is attributed to the remaining readers, is Ali’s reading, and is preferred by Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون فأذنوا مقصورا مفتوح الذال، وهي قراءة علي واختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The short reading means become aware or hear; the verb can mean to hear or know, as in the verse about the earth listening to its Lord.
rows.anchor: فمن قصر معناه: فاعلموا أنتم واسمعوا، يقال: أذن الشيء يأذن أذنا وأذانة إذا سمعه وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The long reading means inform others, as in the verse where people say they have informed God.
rows.anchor: ومن مد معناه: فاعلموا غيركم. قال الله تعالى: قالوا آذناك ما منا من شهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root relates to the ear: bring the matter to people’s hearing.
rows.anchor: وأصل الكلمة من الأذن أي أقعوه في الأذان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that on Judgment Day those who consume usury are told to take up arms for war.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: يقال يوم القيامة لا تأكل الربا: خذ سلاحك للحرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Walibi’s report from Ibn Abbas says a persistent usurer must be asked by the Muslim ruler to repent and, if he refuses, be executed.
rows.anchor: وروى الوالبي عنه قال: من كان مقيما على الربا لا ينزع عنه، فحق على إمام المسلمين أن يستتيبه

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The people of legal and linguistic interpretation say God’s war means fire and the Messenger’s war means the sword.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: حرب الله النار وحرب رسوله السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After repentance, creditors may claim only their principal: demanding more wrongs debtors, while reducing the principal wrongs creditors.
rows.anchor: وإن تبتم فلكم رؤس أموالكم لا تظلمون بطلب الزيادة ولا تظلمون النقصان عن رأس المال

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim, in the transmissions of Aban and al-Mufaddal, reads the two consonants in tubtum with the first ta rounded and the second open.
rows.anchor: وروى آبان والمفضل عن عاصم بضم التاء الأولى وفتح الثانية

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The conditional repentance warns that refusing to repent rejects God’s ruling and makes lawful what He prohibited, rendering the offenders’ property spoils for Muslims.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني أنها شرط التوبة لأنهم أن لم يتوبوا كفروا برد حكم الله واستحلال ما حرم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the revelation, Banu Amr ibn Umayr agreed to repent and accept principal only; Banu al-Mughira pleaded inability to pay until harvest, but their request for delay was refused, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: بل نتوب إلى الله فإنه ليس لنا يدان بحرب الله وحرب رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In wa-in kāna dhū ʿusratin, kāna’s subject is an indefinite noun and its predicate may be omitted; alternatively kāna denotes an event and needs no predicate.
rows.anchor: رفع الكلام باسم كان ولم يأت لها بخبر وذلك جائز في النكرة

rows.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ubayy, Ibn Masud, and Ibn Abbas read dhā ʿusratin, with an implied subject such as the creditor or debtor.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وابن مسعود وابن عباس: إن كان ذا عسرة على إضمار الإسم

rows.speaker: آبان بن عثمان
rows.claim: Aban ibn Uthman reads wa-man kāna dhā ʿusratin li-hādhihi al-ghallah.
rows.anchor: وقرأ آبان بن عثمان: ومن كان ذا عسرة لهذه الغلة

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads wa-in kāna muʿsiran, which the author says supports the standard reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: وإن كان معسر وهو دليل قراءة العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUsrah means poverty, constraint, or hardship; Abu Jaʿfar reads the word with a damma on the sin, another dialect form.
rows.anchor: والعسرة: الفقر والضيق والشدة. وقرأ أبو جعفر: عسرة بضم السين، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-naẓirat is an imperative in the form of a declarative; the conditional fa introduces it, and its meaning is that deferment is obligatory.
rows.anchor: فنظرة أمر في صيغة الخبر، والفاء فيه لجواب الشرط تقديره: فعليه نظرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that the debtor must be given time; making it an accusative command would also be sound, like the command to strike necks.
rows.anchor: أي قال: واجب نظره بالنصب على معنى فلينظر نظرة لكان صوابا كقوله فضرب الرقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naẓirah means granting a delay.
rows.anchor: والنظرة: الإنظار

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Abu Raja, al-Hasan, and Qatada read fa-nāẓirat, a feminine participle meaning one who waits.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء والحسن وقتادة: فناظرة بكسر الضاد ورفع الراء والهاء أي منتظرة

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah reads fa-naẓrah with a still zha; it can be a verbal noun of either looking or waiting.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عطاء بن أبي رباح: فنظرة ساكنة الظاء وهي مصدر يجوز أن يكون من النظر والانتظار جميعا

rows.speaker: عطاء وشيبة ونافع وحميد بن محيص
rows.claim: Ata, Shaybah, Nafi, and Humayd ibn Muhays read maysarah with a damma on the sin and tanwin.
rows.anchor: قرأ عطاء وشيبة ونافع وحميد بن محيص: ميسرة بضم السين والتنوين

rows.speaker: عمر وعلي وأبو رجاء والحسن وقتادة وعبد الله بن مسلم وأبو جعفر وابن كثير وابن عامر وعاصم والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وأيوب
rows.claim: A large group of readers gives maysarah a fatha on the sin with tanwin; Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer it as the common dialect.
rows.anchor: ميسرة بالتنوين وفتح السين وهي اختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم لأنها اللغة السائرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو سراح الهذلي
rows.claim: Mujahid and Abu Sarrah al-Hudhali read maysarah with a damma on the sin in an annexed construction, also transmitted by Zayd from Yaqub.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وأبو سراح الهذلي: (ميسره) بضم السين مضافا هو مثله

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah’s reading is fa-nāẓirūhu ilā maysūrah; all these forms mean wealth, affluence, or spacious ease.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله أنه كان يقرأها: فناظروه إلى ميسورة، وكلها لغات معناها اليسار والغنى والسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving the poor debtor charity means remitting the principal owed; it is better for creditors if they know.
rows.anchor: وأن تصدقوا رؤوس أموالكم على المعسر فلا تطالبونه بها خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Asim reads taṣṣaddaqū with a light ṣad; the other readers pronounce it doubled.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم: تصدقوا بتخفيف الصاد. الباقون بتشديده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An insolvent debtor must be granted time until solvent; the creditor may not demand payment before then, and the debt must be paid in full once solvency appears.
rows.anchor: فلا سبيل لرب المال إلى مطالبته بماله إلى أن يظهر يساره، فإذا ظهر يساره كان عليه توفير الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For debts incurred in exchange for money received, such as a loan or purchase, a debtor claiming insolvency must prove it because receipt establishes an initial presumption of means.
rows.anchor: مثل قرض أو ابتياع سلعة، فإذا ادعى الإعسار لزمته البينة على الإعسار لأن الأصل فيه استغناؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For obligations without money received, such as dowry or guarantee, the creditor must prove the debtor is solvent, since the presumption is that people are poor; absent evidence of prior means, retain the original presumption.
rows.anchor: كالمهر والضمان، فإذا ادعى الإعسار لزم رب المال أمامه البينة على كونه موسرا لأن الأصل في الناس الفقر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says a debtor who declares himself indigent is believed on oath, while creditors must establish his assets by evidence or direct observation.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: إذا قال: أنا معدم، فالقول قوله مع يمينه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa would detain the debtor for two or three months, inquire privately, then release him if insolvency was confirmed.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو حنيفة يرى أن يحبس شهرين أو ثلاثة ثم يسأل عنه في السر

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report from Abu Said al-Khudri supports not imprisoning an insolvent debtor: after a man lost his fruit crop and his debt grew, the Prophet said to take whatever was found, and nothing else was owed.
rows.anchor: حديث أبي سعيد الخدري قال: أصيب رجل في ثمار فكثر دينه، فقال رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: As judge in Medina, Abu Hurayra refused to jail a debtor with no visible property or assets to sell; he should earn for himself and his family and repay when solvent.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو هريرة على قضاء المدينة فأتاه رجل بغريم فقال: أريد أن تحبسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet promised that a person who goes to a debtor to collect his right receives prayers from earthly creatures, a tree in Paradise and forgiveness for every step; a debtor who delays is transgressive.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم)

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet calls a solvent person’s delay in repayment injustice and instructs creditors to accept transfer to a solvent payer.
rows.anchor: أبو الزياد الأعرج عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever gives an insolvent debtor time or remits debt will be shaded by God beneath His Throne on the Day with no other shade.
rows.anchor: زيد بن أسلم عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet says that anyone seeking an answered prayer and relief from distress should make payment easy for the insolvent.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: Hudhayfa recounts that a servant’s only good deed was easing and extending time to an insolvent debtor; God says He is more entitled to do so and forgives the servant. Abu Masud testified that the Prophet had told it.
rows.anchor: ربعي بن خراش عن حذيفة بن اليمان قال: أتى الله عز وجل بعبده يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: بريدة
rows.claim: The Prophet first promised daily charity for each day of deferment before the deadline, then charity equal to the deferred amount for each day after it; Burayda asked about the distinction.
rows.anchor: الأعمش عن أبي داود عن بريدة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: When Jabir found his debtor insolvent, he cited the verse on deferment and erased the debt record.
rows.anchor: أن جابر بن عبد الله خرج إلى غريم له يتقاضاه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن جعفر
rows.claim: The Prophet says God is with a creditor until the debt is paid, provided it is not owed for something God dislikes; Abdullah ibn Jaafar consequently directed his treasurer to collect debts.
rows.anchor: جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن جعفر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet calls a loan taken with no intention of repayment theft.
rows.anchor: عطاء بن يسار عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو قتادة
rows.claim: The Prophet initially declined to pray over a man who owed debt; Abu Qatada guaranteed repayment, so the Prophet asked whether it would be paid and then prayed. The debt was seventeen or eighteen dirhams.
rows.anchor: عثمان بن عبد الله عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه: إن رجلا أتى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: When Abu Said asked whether debt could equal disbelief, the Prophet answered yes after seeking refuge from both.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that debt is God’s banner on earth: when God wills to humble a servant, He tests him with debt bound around his neck.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: After major sins, the gravest sin before God is to die owing people money with no means of repayment.
rows.anchor: وعن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet warns people to avoid debt because it brings anxiety at night and humiliation by day.
rows.anchor: يزيد بن أبي خالد عن ابن أيوب عن أنس بن مالك: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this was the last verse revealed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: سفيان عن عاصم عن الشعبي عن ابن عباس قال: [هذه] آخر آية نزلت على رسول الله

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators report a sequence: after 69:1 the Prophet sought to know when it would occur; Surah al-Nasr then came, and he began asking forgiveness, saying his death had been announced. He feared death, the grave and the terrors of Judgment despite his forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: لما نزلت هذه الآية إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The Prophet lived six months after this, then received the inheritance verse about collateral relatives during the Farewell Pilgrimage; it was called the Summer Verse.
rows.anchor: فعاش رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ستة أشهر ثم لما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The completion-of-religion verse came at Arafat, and the Prophet lived eighty-one days afterward.
rows.anchor: ثم نزل عليه وهو واقف بعرفة اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم الآية فعاش بعدها أحدا وثمانين يوما

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: After the usury verses came the command to fear the Day of Return, the last verse sent down from heaven; the Prophet lived twenty-one days afterward.
rows.anchor: ثم نزلت عليه آيات الربا، ثم نزلت بعدها واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله وهي آخر آية نزلت من السماء

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Prophet lived nine nights after the final verse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: تسع ليال

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومقاتل
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Muqatil say the Prophet died after seven nights, on Monday, two nights into Rabi al-Awwal in 11 AH.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير ومقاتل: سبع ليال ثم مات يوم الإثنين لليلتين خلتا من شهر ربيع الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God shapes each person in the womb as He wills: male or female, short or tall, dark or light, beautiful or unattractive, fortunate or wretched.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يصوركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء ذكرا وأنثى، قصيرا وطويلا، أسودا وأبيضا، حسنا وقبيحا، سعيدا وشقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear, decisive verses are the book’s foundation, on which legal rulings rest; they gather what is lawful and unlawful and lay it out for Muslims.
rows.anchor: هن أم الكتاب أي أصله الذي يعمل عليه في الأحكام ويجمع الحلال والحرام ويفرغ لأهل الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase Mother of the Book covers the Torah, Gospel, and Quran, each serving as a reference for its religious community and being accepted in every region.
rows.anchor: وهن آيات التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن، وفي كل كتاب يرضى به أهل كل دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic uses mother for any excellent, comprehensive reference: the Preserved Tablet, Opening, Mecca, brain, parent, banner, household provider, and essentials such as water and bread.
rows.anchor: والعرب تسمي كل شيء فاضل جامع يكون مرجعا لقوم، كما قيل للوح المحفوظ: أم الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is singular because the verses together form one complete whole, just as God’s speech is one.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال أم الكتاب ولم يقل أمهات الكتب لأن الآيات كلها في تكاملها واجتماعها كالآية الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation takes the phrase to mean one single word, so each item is a mother of the Book, like each of Mary and her son being a sign.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه كلمة واحدة ف هن أم الكتاب كما قال: وجعلنا ابن مريم وأمه آية

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai says uḵar is a plural of uḵrā, left indeclinable because it is shifted from awāḵir, like ʿUmar and Zufar.
rows.anchor: وأخر: جمع أخرى ولم يصرف لأنه معدول عن أواخر، مثل عمر، وزفر وهو قاله الكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations for uḵar’s indeclinability are that it is an adjective like jamʿ and kusaʿ, or that it follows one of two non-declining patterns.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ترك أخراه لأنه نعت مثل جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutashābihāt means verses that resemble one another; Qatada, al-Rabi, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi define decisive verses as those that abrogate and are acted upon.
rows.anchor: متشابهات: تشبه بعضها بعضا، واختلف العلماء في المحكم والمتشابه كليهما فقال قتادة والربيع والضحاك والسدي

rows.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the report through Atiyya from Ibn Abbas, the abrogated verses are mutashabih: they are believed but not acted upon.
rows.anchor: والمتشابه: المنسوخ الذي يؤمن به ولا يعمل به، هي رواية عطية عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s report through Ali ibn Abi Talha defines decisive verses as abrogating rulings, lawful and unlawful matters, limits, duties, commands, and actionable material; the ambiguous include abrogated, reordered, parabolic, and non-actionable passages.
rows.anchor: روى علي ابن أبي طلحة عنه قال: «محكمات القرآن ناسخة، وحلاله، وحرامه، وحدوده، وفرائضه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the decisive verses as the three commandments in al-Anam and their counterpart in al-Isra.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قوله تعالى: منه آيات محكمات قال: هي الثلاث الآيات في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima say decisive verses concern lawful and unlawful matters; everything else is ambiguous and mutually confirms the rest.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وعكرمة: «المحكم: ما فيه من الحلال والحرام وما سوى ذلك متشابه

rows.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Jafar ibn al-Zubayr defines a decisive verse as one that permits only a single interpretation and an ambiguous verse as one that permits several.
rows.anchor: محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير قال: المحكم: ما لا يحتمل من التأويل غير وجه واحد

rows.speaker: ابن زبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr counts the detailed, bounded prophetic stories as decisive, giving verse counts for Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Shuayb, and Moses, and twenty-four verses on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زبير: من المحكم ما ذكر الله تعالى في كتابه من قصص الأنبياء

rows.speaker: ابن زبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr calls repeated stories ambiguous where their wording varies, such as Noah’s command to carry or sail, and the staff called a moving serpent or a manifest serpent.
rows.anchor: والمتشابه: هو ما أختلف به الألفاظ من قصصهم عند التكرير، كما قال في موضع من قصة نوح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view defines decisive verses as those whose interpretation scholars know and whose meaning they understand.
rows.anchor: وإن بعضهم قال: «المحكم: ما عرف العلماء تأويله، وفهموا معناه»

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid recited the verse and said that he is among those who know its interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد هذه الآية وقال: أنا ممن يعلم تأويله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas once said he knew all the Quran except four terms—ghislin, hananan, al-awwah, and al-raqim—but later learned and explained them.
rows.anchor: وروى سماك عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: كل القرآن أعلم ولا أعلم أربعة

rows.speaker: عائشة وعروة بن الزبير وطاوس عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They treat the waw before those firmly rooted in knowledge as starting a new sentence: only God knows the interpretation, while the learned affirm belief; al-Kisai, al-Farra, al-Mufaddal ibn Salama, and Ibn Jarir choose this reading.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: الواو في قوله والراسخون في العلم واو الاستئناف وتم الكلام

rows.speaker: عائشة وعروة بن الزبير وطاوس عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: On this reading, the unknowable interpretation concerns the appointed time of the Hour, the world’s end, the sun rising in the west, Jesus, the Dajjal, Gog and Magog, the spirit, and other matters God reserves.
rows.anchor: والآية راجعة على هذا التأويل الى العلم بما في أجل هذه الأمة ووقت قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says God has reserved knowledge of the ambiguous material and people are not charged with interpreting it, but are charged to obey commands and avoid prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أستأثر الله بعلمه دوننا، ونفسره نحن، ولم نتعبد بذلك. بل ألزمنا العمل بأوامره واجتناب نواهيه

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Abdullah places the phrase only with God, then begins a new statement that those firmly rooted in knowledge say they believe.
rows.anchor: قراءة عبد الله أن تأويله لا يعلم إلا عند الله، والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said the knowledge of the firmly rooted ends at their affirmation that everything comes from their Lord.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن عمر بن عبد العزيز، إنه قرأ هذه الآية ثم قال: انتهى علم الراسخين في العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Nuhaik says readers wrongly join the phrase to the preceding clause; the author judges separation more grammatical and closer to the apparent wording and context.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو نهيك الأسدي: إنكم تصلون هذه الآية وإنها مقطوعة وهذا القول أقيس العربية وأشبه مظاهر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those firmly rooted are deeply established in knowledge, having perfected and derived it so that doubt does not enter their understanding; the word denotes something firmly fixed.
rows.anchor: والراسخون: الداخلون في العلم الذين أتقنوا علمهم، واستنبطوه فلا يدخلهم في معرفتهم شك

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The author notes paired forms rasakha and raṣakha, alongside maslūkh and maṣlūkh, as Arabic usage examples.
rows.anchor: فهو يرسخ رسخا ورسوخا وكذلك في كل شيء ورسخ رصخ

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify those firmly rooted in knowledge as believing People of the Book, including Abdullah ibn Salam, Ibn Surayya, and Kaʿb.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين من العلماء: الراسخون علما: مؤمني أهل الكتاب، مثل عبد الله بن سلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the firmly rooted as some of those learned in Torah.
rows.anchor: [قيل:] الراسخون في العلم هم بعض الدارسين علم التوراة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك وأبو الدرداء وأبو أمامة
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet defined the firmly rooted as people with truthful oaths and speech, upright hearts, and chaste appetites and sexuality.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أنس بن مالك [وأبي الدرداء وأبي أمامة] : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل من الراسخون في العلم

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik ibn Anas says the firmly rooted person is a scholar who acts on what he knows and follows that knowledge.
rows.anchor: سمعت مالك بن أنس يسأل عن تفسير قوله والراسخون في العلم من هم؟ قال: العالم العامل بما علم

rows.speaker: نافع بن يزيد
rows.claim: Nafi ibn Yazid describes them as believers humbled in seeking God’s pleasure, neither arrogant toward superiors nor contemptuous toward inferiors.
rows.anchor: وقال نافع بن يزيد: كما أن يقال الراسخون في العلم المؤمنون بالله، المتذللون في طلب مرضاته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another account says the firmly rooted embody four traits: piety toward God, humility toward people, asceticism toward worldly life, and struggle against the self.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الراسخون في العلم: من وجد في عمله أربعة أشياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: They say God names them firmly rooted because they affirm belief in all ambiguous and decisive material, abrogating and abrogated, whether understood or not, as all comes from their Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي بقولهم: (آمنا به) سماهم الله تعالى: الراسخين في العلم

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says some grammarians treat ʿinda in all is from our Lord as an extra particle, so the sense is simply all is from our Lord.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: زعم بعض الناس أن (عند) هاهنا صلة ومعناه كل من ربنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only people with sound intellect take heed; lubb is the pure core of anything, which is why intellect is called lubb.
rows.anchor: إلا أولوا الألباب: ذووا العقول ولب كل شيء خالصه
